data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise advanced passive structures including reporting passives, modal passives and passive infinitive and gerund forms.
learningPoints: Use passive forms across a range of tenses and modal structures.
Use reporting passives such as 'It is believed that...' and 'He is believed to...'.
Use perfect passive forms with have been + past participle.
Recognise passive infinitive and gerund structures.
Choose passive structures when the action or result is more important than the agent.

words.word: The form must be completed by Friday.
The form must completed by Friday.
The form must be complete by Friday, when an action is intended.

sections.explain: Use HAVE/HAS BEEN + past participle for Present Perfect passive forms.

words.word: The documents have been sent.
The documents have sent.
The documents have been send.

sections.explain: IT IS BELIEVED THAT is a formal reporting passive.

words.word: It is believed that the company will expand.
It believes that the company will expand.
It is believe that the company will expand.

sections.explain: A person or thing can become the subject of a reporting passive: SUBJECT + BE + believed/said/thought + TO.

words.word: The actor is said to live in Paris.
The actor is said that he lives in Paris.
The actor said to live in Paris.

sections.summary: Using a perfect infinitive after a reporting passive.
sections.explain: Use TO HAVE + past participle when the reported action happened earlier.

words.word: He is believed to have left the country.
He is believed to left the country.
He is believed having left the country.

sections.explain: Use TO BE + past participle in a passive infinitive.

words.word: The equipment needs to be checked regularly.
The equipment needs to checked regularly.
The equipment needs being check regularly.

sections.explain: Use BEING + past participle after verbs or prepositions that require a gerund.

words.word: She dislikes being told what to do.
She dislikes to be told what to do in this gerund pattern.
She dislikes being tell what to do.

sections.explain: Use WILL HAVE BEEN + past participle for something completed in passive form before a future point.

words.word: By June, the new bridge will have been completed.
By June, the new bridge will have completed.
By June, the new bridge will have been complete.

sections.explain: GET + past participle is common in less formal contexts, often for events affecting the subject.

words.word: He got promoted last month.
He got promote last month.
He was got promoted last month.

sections.summary: Using passive focus in formal writing.
sections.explain: The passive is useful when the process or result is more important than the agent.

words.word: Several changes were introduced following the review.
Several changes introduced following the review.
Several changes were introduce following the review.
